title: Probabilistic gatekeeper for canary, A/B and shadow traffic
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Build a probabilistic gatekeeper service that synthesizes multiple SLO signals (latency P95/P99, 5xx error rate, token cost deviation, throughput headroom) and emits graded action signals for canary/A-B and shadow deployments. The gatekeeper should support gradual annealing of thresholds, per-cohort baselining, and integrate with Redwood's rollout controller to optionally trigger automated rollback, traffic reweighting, or pause escalation. Goal: reduce false-positive evacuations for transient noise while still providing fast protection for real regressions.
acceptance_criteria: Gatekeeper can consume metric streams (latency/error/throughput/cost) from Console tracing and evaluate a combined risk score in <200ms per evaluation
Risk scoring model supports configurable weights and a Bayesian annealing policy that transitions from permissive -> conservative over a configurable warmup window
Default policy prevents auto-rollback for single-metric spikes under 3 minutes unless risk score > 0.9, while still allowing immediate rollback for sustained multi-signal breaches

Integration tests verifying: (a) canary with synthetic latency spike triggers traffic cut to 0% within configured SLA; (b) shadow traffic anomaly logs but does not affect live traffic when configured as observation-only
Dashboard in Console shows per-canary risk score timeline, contributing signals, and explainability hints (which metric pushed score)
engineering_notes: Design choice: probabilistic aggregate score vs deterministic rule set. Probabilistic reduces brittle thresholds but requires more telemetry for calibration.
We will use an ensemble of lightweight detectors: EWMA drift, change-point detection (CUSUM), and a Bayesian posterior over expected baseline to compute a posterior probability of regression.
Trade-off: heavier detectors (e.g., full Bayesian changepoint) are more accurate but increase CPU on control plane. Aim for <2 vCPU steady-state per 100 concurrent canaries.
Cohort baselining: compute baseline per-customer/region/model-version where traffic volume allows; otherwise fallback to global baseline with wider confidence intervals.
Token-cost signal: compare per-token real cost vs expected cost for same prompt mix; normalize by median prompt length to avoid noisy cost spikes from outliers.
Rollback actions: (1) 'soft-reduce' traffic reweight by factor, (2) 'pause' rollout (no further increases), (3) 'evacuate' full rollback. Gatekeeper outputs recommended action and confidence.
We must provide manual override & audit log for all auto actions (security/compliance requirement).
progress_updates: 2026-02-20: Epic created and scope agreed with PM. Initial exploration of statistical techniques completed.
2026-02-26: Prototype risk score lambda implemented using EWMA + simple z-score thresholding (proof-of-concept). Repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-safety/tree/eng/ENG-98890
2026-03-02: Architecture review with infra: decided to host gatekeeper as control-plane microservice behind rollout-controller; API contract drafted: /evaluate, /explain, /act

2026-03-05: Spike results: Bayesian annealing reduced false positives by ~45% on historical canary traces (internal test harness). Notebook: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/ml/eng/ENG-98890/annealing-spike.ipynb
2026-03-08: Security review requested; noted requirement for KMS-encrypted audit logs and RBAC on act endpoints. Security PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/security/pull/514
2026-03-10: First integration test passes for synthetic latency regression scenario. Preparing RFC for canary policy schema changes.
decisions: Adopt Bayesian annealing as default tuning method for warmups (reason: graceful tightening of thresholds reduces unnecessary rollbacks during cold start)
Expose per-signal weights in rollout policy with sane defaults (latency: 0.4, error-rate: 0.35, throughput: 0.15, token-cost: 0.1). Weights adjustable by tenant via policy override.
Auto-rollback will be enabled only for 'evacuate' action and only for customers who opted-in; default is 'pause' + alert for hosted customers to avoid surprise rollbacks.
Gatekeeper explainability: return top-2 contributing signals and a short human-readable rationale string for Console display.
review_feedback: PM (Mar 03): Request to add customer-impact tagging so ops can filter critical customers and adjust sensitivity.
SRE (Mar 04): Concern about evaluation load at scale; suggested batched evaluations and caching of recent risk scores per canary.
Design (Mar 06): UX needs explicit timeline and ability to replay canary events in Console for post-mortem — added to acceptance criteria.
Security (Mar 08): Require HMAC on act endpoints and immutable signed audit entries for any auto-action.
